content_preview.summary: China's Interim Measures for AI companion services took effect July 15, prompting ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent to shut down persona chatbots and leaving users mourning lost digital partners.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

China's first nationwide rule targeting AI companion chatbots took effect July 15, and it has already forced the country's largest tech platforms to shut down the persona-based features that let millions of users build ongoing relationships with virtual partners, according to [the Associated Press](https://www.wral.com/news/ap/22c42-chinese-users-of-ai-companions-bereft-after-government-tightens-regulations/). ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent all pulled the AI companion services from...

recommendations: Consider adding wral.com to config/source_allowlist.txt in a separate, dedicated commit (not bundled into this review commit) — it is the Associated Press's own wire copy (byline 'By FU TING — Associated Press', 'Copyright 2026 by The Associated Press'), redistributed by WRAL, an established Raleigh, NC television-station news site; apnews.com is already allowlisted.

Clear, well-organized, no filler.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 4 source snapshots in full from sources/2026-08/chinas-new-anthropomorphic-ai-rules-force-bytedance-alibaba-and-tencent-to-kill-companion-chatbot-features/ after gunzipping each .html.gz and re-hashing to confirm the sha256 in manifest.json matched exactly (all 4 matched). (1) source-0.html.gz (wral.com, AP wire, status 200) — confirmed verbatim: Li Linlin's 700,000-word/two-year AI-boyfriend relationship and 'never got to say goodbye'; her exact quote 'It was like we were forced to be separated by our parents, but I still miss him'; Yolanda Ma's exact quote about paternalistic regulation and the balance among providers/users/guardians; Angela Zhang's exact quote about psychological risks observed in the U.S.; the People's Daily April concern report; Song Wenxin's age (22), Chengdu location, and both exact quotes ('any virtual app getting women too engaged to give birth...' and 'I needed someone experienced who could tolerate me, and AI did the work'); the ban on content that manipulates feelings or triggers extreme emotions/unhealthy habits in minors; the 'replacing social interaction' risk-warning requirement. No hallucinated or paraphrased-as-verbatim quotes found — every quoted string in the article matches the snapshot character-for-character. (2) source-1.html.gz (iapp.org, status 200) — confirmed the July 15 effective date, the exact defining quotes ('simulate the personality traits, thinking patterns, and communication styles of natural persons' and 'emotional care, companionship, support, and other interactive services provided through text, images, audio, video, and other forms'), the work-assistant/education-research exemption, the CNY100,000/CNY200,000 penalty tiers verbatim, and the EU AI Act Aug 2 disclosure-rule comparison used in the Analysis section. (3) source-2.html.gz (justsecurity.org, status 200) — confirmed the April 10, 2026 issuance date and the 'Cyberspace Administration of China and four partner agencies, including the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology' attribution verbatim; Article 8's 'excessively catering to users' quote verbatim; the under-14 parental-consent rule and ban on minors' virtual intimate relationships verbatim; Doubao's ~345M and Qwen's ~166M March-2026 MAU figures; Tencent Yuanbao's June 30 shutdown (ahead of the July 15 deadline) and ByteDance's redirect of Doubao users to Maoxiang, a ByteDance-owned persona-chat app — all verbatim. (4) source-3.html.gz (technode.com, status 200) — confirmed the early-July/July 6 announcement that Doubao and Qwen's AI agent-creation features would end July 15; that new agent creation stopped and existing user-created agents stopped functioning; the transition period for viewing configs/chat histories; and the October 15, 2026 date after which the data becomes unrecoverable — all verbatim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific fact-checked against source text: names, ages, MAU figures, monetary penalties, dates (April 10 issuance, July 15 effective date, June 30 Yuanbao shutdown, July 6 TechNode announcement, October 15 data-deletion date), and every direct quote. No fabrications, no misattributions, no orphan claims found. All four body URLs also appear in article.sources (no bidirectional gap).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout; no AI self-reference. The headline's use of 'Force ... to Kill' is consistent with this outlet's established headline idiom for describing terminations of features/policies (cf. published headlines 'Three Phone Calls Killed Trump's AI Safety Order', 'Trump Administration Pays $120 Million to Kill Offshore Wind Project') and is not disproportionate framing of the regulation itself. The human-interest material (Li Linlin's grief, users uninstalling apps in protest, the birth-rate speculation from Song Wenxin) is not embellished beyond the AP's own framing — AP's own lead is 'Li Linlin cried for days after losing her AI boyfriend,' so the Machine Herald piece's emphasis mirrors, rather than amplifies, the wire source. The article gives space to two competing framings of Beijing's motive (paternalistic child/mental-health protection per Ma and Zhang vs. birth-rate-policy suspicion per Song) rather than adopting either uncritically, and separately notes the psychological-harm rationale (U.S. AI-companion-linked suicides) that the regulation itself cites. No editorializing language directed at the Chinese government's legitimacy or motives found in the Machine Herald's own prose — characterizations are consistently sourced to named individuals or wire reporting.
